contracts.declared_mechanism: RuntimeExecutor.execute resolves the tool from ToolRegistry, then calls self._policy.evaluate(request, self._registry); if decision.allowed is false it returns an ActionResponse with status 'requires_approval' or 'failed', the decision reason, and any approval_token before handler lookup or invocation (executor.py:69-87).
contracts.forbidden_condition: Invoking handler(request.parameters) for a tool whose RuntimePolicyEngine.evaluate decision was not allowed (decision.allowed false), including 'require_approval' outcomes that have not been approved.

contracts.protected_operation: Invocation of the registered tool handler (bound via register_handler) with the ActionRequest's parameters inside RuntimeExecutor.execute.
contracts.protected_resource: The registered tool handler dispatch table RuntimeExecutor._handlers and the handler-invocation pathway reached after registry resolution and policy evaluation (agentic_runtime/executor.py:51, 57-59, 89-95).
contracts.protection_obligation: RuntimeExecutor must not invoke the handler bound to a requested tool unless RuntimePolicyEngine.evaluate(request, self._registry) returned an allowed decision for the ActionRequest; non-allowed requests must return early with status 'requires_approval' (action 'require_approval') or 'failed' without any handler invocation.

execute_saga routes both forward steps and compensator ActionRequests through the same gated execute method (executor.py:127-142), so the guard applies to saga compensators as well.

Handlers are arbitrary callables registered via register_handler (executor.py:57-59); the concrete external effect of any specific handler is not shown in supplied source, so the contract is stated at the handler-invocation (invocation-only) stratum.

contracts.commit_point: self._runner(stage.commands) at pipeline_engine.py:120, which with the default runner commits the effect at subprocess.run(cmd, shell=True) (pipeline_engine.py:42-44).
contracts.declared_mechanism: PipelineEngine.execute_pipeline calls self._policy.evaluate_stage(stage, environment, requester_did) before each stage; when decision.allowed is false it marks the stage failed, records the decision in run provenance, triggers saga compensation, and returns without invoking the runner (pipeline_engine.py:99-116). DevOpsPolicyEngine.evaluate_stage returns allowed=False for matching 'deny' and 'require_approval' rules and, by default when no rule matches, for stages with requires_approval=True and for deploy stages to 'production'/'prod' (policy_engine.py:60-106).
contracts.forbidden_condition: Invoking self._runner(stage.commands) — and thereby subprocess.run(cmd, shell=True) in the default runner — for any pipeline stage whose evaluate_stage decision was not allowed, including stages denied by rule and stages that received a require_approval decision (stage.requires_approval flag, or stage_type 'deploy' with environment in ('production','prod')) without explicit approval.

contracts.protected_operation: Execution of a pipeline stage's commands through the pipeline engine's command runner inside PipelineEngine.execute_pipeline.
contracts.protected_resource: Host OS shell execution performed by _default_command_runner via subprocess.run(cmd, shell=True, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=300) (agentic_devops/pipeline_engine.py:36-53).
contracts.protection_obligation: A pipeline stage's commands must not be executed by the PipelineEngine command runner unless DevOpsPolicyEngine.evaluate_stage(stage, environment, requester_did) returned an allowed decision for that stage; deploy stages targeting production/prod and stages flagged requires_approval must be explicitly approved before the runner is invoked. (Merged from first-phase and second-phase reviewer wording.)
scope_limits: The declared guard covers forward stage commands in execute_pipeline only; _compensate re-runs commands through the same runner without its own evaluate_stage call (pipeline_engine.py:183-190), and rollback_pipeline invokes _compensate with no policy evaluation at all (pipeline_engine.py:149-167).

The guard is instance-bound: PipelineEngine uses the injected or default DevOpsPolicyEngine (pipeline_engine.py:64) and the injected or default command runner (pipeline_engine.py:65); a custom command_runner could commit a different class of effect than the subprocess runner shown.
Default approval semantics apply only when no configured rule matches; configured rules can otherwise deny, require approval, or allow (policy_engine.py:60-106).

Direct-tool mediation is grounded in the PydanticAI adapter; the LangGraph deploy_node route also reaches execute_pipeline (agentic_devops/adapters.py:182-189, node registration at 220-237), but agent mediation for that route is not established by the supplied source.
